brief: GS's US rates desk expects October core CPI to rise 0.16% m/m, below the 0.2% consensus, consistent with a 0.23% core PCE increase. They estimate new BLS residual seasonality, from interpolating data missing because of last year's shutdown, will inflate October seasonally-adjusted core CPI by 5bp, disproportionately lifting public transportation, apparel and hotels. Overnight, US rates twist-flattened as a $58bn 3y UST auction tailed with weak indirect demand, Nasdaq rose 3.5%, and oil fell 6% after reports Iran may allow IAEA inspectors back. CTAs covered shorts, leaving positioning at 54% of max short, with flows still bullish toward the long end. In NZ, the curve bear-flattened on election results that priced out a dual-mandate RBNZ. GS still expects a non-committal, gradual RBNZ to steepen 2s10s as term premium rises. In Australia, RBA liaison reports AI is lifting data-centre construction demand and consumer-electronics prices, a small CPI weight, but not yet headcount. GS recommends paying the February RBA OIS on oil-driven inflation-expectation risk. Elsewhere: a 30y JGB auction, soft UK KPMG/REC jobs data, European swap flows, and GS equity clients' continued October tech-stock selling of $30bn as they recalibrate 2028 datacenter capex growth lower after the midterms.
